title: canopy-fanout-progressive-delta-rollback-protocol
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Adds a coordinated canopy fanout rollout controller with progressive delta rollback policy; new 'canopy' rollout config field; dry-run validation mode; telemetry hooks for session-cohort drift; docs and migration guide.
description:
Summary: Implements a new coordinated "canopy" fanout rollout controller and a progressive-delta rollback protocol to safely promote model variants across mixed cohorts and shadow lanes. Motivation: existing canary and shadow patterns work well individually but teams running interleaved A/B + shadow experiments reported edge cases where session affinity, downstream cache priming, and cross-cohort signal leakage caused noisy metrics that delayed rollbacks or produced false positives. This PR introduces a coarse-grained canopy fanout strategy that partitions traffic into logical leaves (cohorts, shadows, rehearse lanes) and applies a delta-based regression detector that triggers stepwise rollback credits rather than an immediate global backout.

What changed (high level): commits include: 1) rollout/controller: add canopy-fanout controller orchestration with state machine and lease-based cohort handshake; 2) rollout/policy: progressive-delta rollback policy implementation and scoring; 3) runtime/router: session-affinity extension to support canopy leaves and sticky shadow mappings; 4) telemetry: new prometheus counters and verbose smoke-replay traces for leaf reconciliation; 5) cli/docs: rollout migration guide and example configs; 6) tests: unit and integration harness for dry-run and simulated drift; 7) e2e: small canary scenario harness with replayable traffic snapshots. Files touched (representative): rollout/controller/canopy_controller.go, rollout/policy/delta_rollback.go, runtime/router/sticky_map.go, telemetry/canopy_metrics.yaml, docs/rollouts/canopy.md, examples/rollouts/canopy-example.yaml, test/harness/canopy_sim.py, ci/rollout-smoke.yml.

Key behaviors and safety model: - Canopy partitions are declared in the rollout spec under a new "canopy" stanza. Leaves can be cohorts, shadow lanes, or rehearse lanes; each leaf has a weight, affinity rules, and an isolation policy. - Progressive-delta rollback evaluates multi-metric deltas against historical baselines and applies a crediting model: small regressions deduct credits from a leaf; when credits exhaust, leaf is removed and traffic redistributed incrementally. - Session-cohort reconciliation ensures user/session affinity is respected during stepwise weight changes and supports rewind via snapshot-backed replay for affected sessions. - Dry-run mode validates rollout plan by simulating fanout and collecting smoke metrics without committing traffic changes. - Telemetry emits leaf-level trace IDs and smoothed deltas for downstream automated gating and manual playbooks.

Backward compatibility and migration: rollout API remains backward compatible; existing canary specs still work. There's a minor schema extension to accept "canopy" in the rollout spec; servers will ignore unknown fields when speaking to older agents. Migration guide added at docs/rollouts/canopy.md with recommended staged rollout steps. No customer visible breaking changes expected.

Tests and CI: Added unit tests for delta scoring, session-affinity preservation, and controller failover. Integration test simulates a mixed A/B + shadow workload and verifies rollback credit behavior under noisy metrics. Initial CI run showed a flaky timeout in test/harness/canopy_sim.py on the first run (integration smoke). I addressed it by increasing test harness timeouts and adding a deterministic replay seed; subsequent CI reruns passed all checks (build, lint, unit, integration, e2e smoke).

Review conversation (abridged, single thread style): - Liam O'Neill: "High-level looks good; need clarity on credit decay math and potential for long tail false positives. Please add docs for the scoring function and a default safe threshold." - Priya (author): "Added detailed scoring doc section, default thresholds tuned to historical baselines; added test vectors and explanation in canopy.md." - Maya Chen: "Concerned about cross-region routing when a leaf is evicted; how do we avoid hotspotting?" - Priya: "Controller now honors region affinity and will rebalance across compatible leaves with a warmup smoothing factor; documented behavior and added a test case." - Diego Alvarez: "Suggest logging an audit event when a leaf exhausts credits for easier post-incident analysis." - Priya: "Added auditable event emission to telemetry and included a small console hook in rollout CLI for on-call." - Liam: "Approve after CI is green and the migration doc includes rollback playbook." - Final: approved by Liam and Maya; Diego left a comment-only approval.

Operational notes and playbook snippets: - To try in dry-run: `redwoodctl rollout apply --file examples/rollouts/canopy-example.yaml --dry-run` - To promote: apply with `--commit` and watch canopy leaf metrics under telemetry/canopy_metrics.yaml; the controller exposes an api `/rollouts/{id}/state` for manual intervention. - If a leaf is evicted, controller emits `rollout.leaf.evict` with reason and a snapshot id for possible rewind/replay.

Example rollout snippet (from examples/rollouts/canopy-example.yaml):

rollout:
  name: experimental-chat-model-canopy
  type: canopy
  leaves:
    - name: cohort-a
      weight: 30
      affinity:
        region: us-west1
    - name: shadow-rehearse
      weight: 0
      mode: shadow
  policy:
    rollback: progressive-delta
    thresholds:
      latency_ms: 1.25
      regression_score: 0.02

Why this is different: Unlike a monolithic canary this controller reasons about coordinated leaves (a canopy) that can contain mixed modes (A/B + shadow + rehearse), enforces session-cohort consistency during traffic shifts, and uses a credited progressive rollback to reduce blast radius while still enabling automated rollback when metrics truly degrade.

Follow-ups (planned): - ENG-5023: expose per-leaf detailed timelines in Console for on-call analysis. - ENG-5060: automatic replay-based bisect when a leaf's credits deplete to help pinpoint offending input slices. - small perf tune to the router sticky_map under extremely high concurrency (bench in perf lab queued).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after two approvals and green CI. Deploy gating: Controller gated behind feature flag `rollout.canopy=true` for staged rollout to production clusters. Rollout flagged enabled in staging on 2026-03-09 for live smoke testing.
